questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the street.
questions.explanation: Drive with caution around children. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Make it take longer to stop.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires make it harder to turn, increase your stopping distance, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When driving on a gravel or dirt road, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down on gravel or dirt roads. It takes much longer to stop on these surfaces than on paved roads, and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If the crossing gate is down.
If the crossing lights are flashing red.

questions.explanation: Always stop at railroad crossings if flashing red lights are on, the crossing gate is down, a stop sign is posted, or a train is close. When in doubt, stop. Never race a train.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Stop and move your vehicle off the road if possible. Check for injuries and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if anyone is hurt or if there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Drive better because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers doing these things lose control of their vehicles and drift out of their lanes.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, wait until the entire car is visible in your rearview mirror before moving back to the right lane.
questions.explanation: Do not return to the right lane until you can see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Drivers and cyclists must be extra alert at night to prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: They drive slower than other traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, jerking motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: Drivers must be careful when passing large vehicles and should not drive beside them for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive next to a large vehicle for a long time. It is safer to either slow down or speed up to move away from it.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when:

options.text: You reach an intersection with a stop sign.
A traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop when approaching a stop sign, approaching a red light, or when a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns drivers of upcoming hazards. It tells you a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: You are driving when it starts to rain. You should:

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive closely behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: When rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the shoulder and stop until it improves.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. If you are on a two-lane road and traffic is backing up behind you, pull off the road to let other vehicles pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This "Keep right" sign means a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch for standing water or puddles.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars take longer to stop and may skid on turns. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You are more likely to survive a car crash if you wear both lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should fit snugly across your hips or upper thighs. The shoulder belt should fit snugly across your chest and shoulder. Properly positioned seat belts greatly reduce injury in a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: To change lanes safely, signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: You cannot pass another vehicle on:
questions.explanation: You cannot pass on hills, curves, intersections, or railroad crossings. These places are unsafe for passing.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It helps driving skills but harms judgment.
It harms both driving skills and judgment.
It has no effect on either driving skills or judgment.
It harms driving skills but not judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It harms both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it hard to see clearly. It also makes you misjudge speed and distance, and makes you more likely to take dangerous risks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: Many crashes happen because:

options.text: Drivers go too fast for conditions.
Drivers check mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers give the right-of-way to others.
Drivers keep a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers go too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers speed. Always follow the speed limit and slow down when conditions are bad.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes. Only stop on the shoulder in emergencies. Avoid using cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather. Change lanes only when necessary.

questions.question: After being stopped by police, you should immediately exit your vehicle and quickly approach the officer.
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle with both hands visible on the steering wheel when stopped by police.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way when crossing at an intersection. A crosswalk exists at any intersection, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, around pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if it goes against the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and be careful in school zones, even if a guard is not present.

questions.question: When you meet an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is driving dangerously, stay calm and create distance between your vehicles. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make gestures.
